report.summary: Chunk 9 of 11 of canary.py: defines grade() return logic, _run_lane() and run_canary() functions with docstrings and comments.
risks: _run_lane | medium | Catches BaseException which includes SystemExit and KeyboardInterrupt; may suppress critical signals. | Confirm if such broad catch is intentional and if any re-raise logic exists elsewhere.

handoff.purpose: Contains the grade() return logic, _run_lane() function, and run_canary() function with docstrings and comments.

symbols.name: _run_lane
symbols.note: Runs one lane's probes sequentially in one thread. Uses gate semaphore and catches BaseException.

symbols.name: run_canary
symbols.note: Main entry point to probe every lane. Raises LiveCanaryRefused if not live and live egress lanes exist.

claims.text: Sequential within a lane on purpose: four concurrent calls to the same vendor is a load test, not a health check, and it would make the latency numbers -- the thing the trailing median compares -- meaningless. It is also what keeps a hung vendor to ONE occupied slot rather than four.
claims.why: The code loops sequentially over probes and boxes with a for loop inside the gate context, no parallelism within a lane.

claims.text: a lane must never take the canary down
claims.why: The code catches BaseException to prevent any exception from propagating.

claims.text: Threads are DAEMONS and are ABANDONED at the wall clock rather than joined: a thread cannot be killed, so a hung vendor must degrade the report instead of blocking it.
claims.why: The chunk does not include the thread creation code to verify daemon or join behavior.

claims.text: Every abandoned (lane, probe) is still reported -- as timeout/wall_clock -- because a silently dropped row is indistinguishable from a probe that was never scheduled.
claims.why: The chunk does not include the logic that collects results for abandoned probes.

claims.text: live is the SPEND OPT-IN and defaults to False. Any lane that still carries a shipped vendor transport (:func:live_egress_lanes) raises :class:LiveCanaryRefused here -- before the run id, before a nonce, before a thread, before one byte is dispatched, and therefore before there is anything for :func:append_history to write. Fake lanes are unaffected, so the offline harness never has to ask for permission it does not need.
claims.why: The code checks `if not live:` and calls `live_egress_lanes(lanes)`; if seats, raises LiveCanaryRefused before any other actions.

claims.text: Materialised ONCE, before anything inspects it: the gate below iterates the roster, and a one-shot iterator would arrive here full, be drained by the gate, and reach the scheduling loop empty -- a canary of no lanes, reported as if it had run.
claims.why: The code does `lanes = tuple(lanes)` to materialize the iterable before any use.

observations.what: In _run_lane, the try block catches BaseException, which includes SystemExit and KeyboardInterrupt, potentially swallowing critical signals.
The run_canary docstring claims threads are daemons but the chunk does not show thread creation; this is uncheckable.
The run_canary docstring claims abandoned probes are reported as timeout/wall_clock, but the code in this chunk does not implement that reporting.
